Hi Liam / Emma —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Below is a concise recap from our discovery and the cost/TCO levers we specifically called out that map to the constraints you described. I tried to keep this tight so we can move to a pilot decision quickly.

TL;DR (ask): You want to reduce per-transaction inference cost enough to support a 3x–5x expansion in message volume over the next 6 months while maintaining P99 latency under ~150ms for the fraud-check route. Budget sensitivity: target monthly spend ceiling ~$45k for inference.

Key pain points we heard
- High token burn during end-of-month reconciliation spikes (burst concurrency).
- Current system can't absorb 2–3x spike without serious cost increase.
- Need deterministic latency for the fraud-check path (customer-facing); other async routes can tolerate higher latency.

Goals we aligned on
- Primary: 3–5x reduction in per-transaction inference cost on high-volume, non-latency-critical flows.
- Secondary: keep fraud-check P99 <= 150ms and preserve quality for critical decisions.
- Pilot target: demonstrate 40–60% unit-cost reduction within 2–3 weeks of ingesting sample traffic.

Concrete levers mapped to your stack
1) Micro-batching with adaptive windows — combine low-latency batch strategies for the non-critical flows to reduce per-token overhead while preserving P99 on fraud checks via routing.
2) Prefix/KV caching — many reconciliation prompts share repeated prefixes; a cache hit rate of 30% could reduce tokens served by ~20–30%.
3) Quantized model variant for low-risk scoring — run a 4-bit quantized variant for background enrichment and use higher-precision model for fraud-checks.
4) Model routing & fallbacks — route low-criticality traffic to lower-cost models or shorter-context variants; keep fallback to full model when confidence is low.
5) Reserved throughput / commit discounts — evaluate a small reserved pool (e.g., 2 GPU equivalent commit) to get predictable unit pricing during spikes.

Initial pilot proposal (what we'd do next)
- Scope: host two routes on Redwood Dedicated for 2 weeks: (A) fraud-check (latency SLO) on standard model; (B) enrichment/reconciliation pipeline on quantized + batching + cache.
- Inputs from you: 10k anonymized sample prompts + token distribution, a short list of 10 canonical fraud-check examples for eval.
- Success criteria: 40%+ average cost reduction on route B; fraud-check P99 <= 150ms and no meaningful false-positive regression on the 10 canonical cases.
- Deliverables: cost projection worksheet, pilot runbook, and an ops checklist for production rollout.

Attachments: redwood-econ-playbook.pdf (pilot levers & expected lift), payrise-pilot-scope.xlsx (initial scope + budget sensitivity grid)

Open questions (please confirm)
- Is the $45k/month ceiling a hard cap for Q2 pilot, or is there flexibility for a short test burst?
- Can you provide a sanitized sample of the reconciliation prompts (10k) by EOD Thursday?
- Any regulatory or data residency constraints we should pre-wire into the pilot (SOC2, encryption requirements)?

Next steps
- If you're comfortable, can we schedule a 60-minute working session this week where we walk through the playbook and I’ll run a quick back-of-envelope cost model tailored to your token distribution? You can pick a slot here: https://calendly.com/soojin-lee/40min

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the pilot worksheet in a separate email.

Regards,
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — this is very helpful and in the right level of detail. A couple quick items: 

1) The $45k is a hard cap for Q2 unless we get executive sign-off; we can make room for a two-week pilot if the forecast shows clear upside.
2) We can provide a sanitized dump of 8k–12k reconciliation prompts (PII redacted) — target to share by Thu COB.
3) Security: SOC2 type II required, and logs need to remain in our US tenant; I know you mentioned private deployment options — can you confirm the pilot will respect that?

Small requests for the cost sheet you mentioned:
- Can you add a column that projects spend under 3 traffic scenarios (steady, 2x spike, 3x spike) and include per-route latency impact?
- Curious to see a quick sensitivity to batch size: what happens to P99 if we increase batch size to gain efficiency?

If you can get the pilot worksheet before Thu midday, I’ll run it with Emma and our infra lead and should be ready to confirm calendar slots.

—Liam
Director of Engineering | Payrise Labs
liam.oconnor@payrise.com
